paragraphs.title: A Plea for Judgment and Examination of the Heart

answers: The LORD
His enemies
His children
easy.explanation: David begins by calling upon the LORD to hear his prayer.
easy.q: To whom does David direct his prayer?

answers: His wealth
His heart
His kingdom
easy.explanation: David says, “Thou hast proved mine heart.”
easy.q: What does David say God has proved?

answers: His enemies
His riches
His goings
easy.explanation: He asks God, “Hold up my goings in thy paths.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to hold up?

answers: So that God may judge what is right
So that David may gain riches
So that he can hide from his enemies
medium.explanation: David asks God to behold “the things that are equal,” or what is right.
medium.q: Why does David ask for his sentence to come from God's presence?

answers: His prayer is spoken sincerely
His prayer is whispered secretly
His prayer is spoken angrily
medium.explanation: “Feigned lips” would be deceitful lips, but David claims that his prayer is genuine.
medium.q: What does David mean when he says his prayer does not come from “feigned lips”?

answers: He claims that his heart has been tested and that his mouth will not transgress
He says that he refuses to speak at all
He says that his mouth is wiser than his heart
medium.explanation: God has tested David's heart, and David is purposed not to sin with his mouth.
medium.q: How are David's heart and mouth connected in these verses?

answers: God examines David even in private and unseen times
David slept through God's judgment
David was traveling at night to escape
challenge.explanation: The verse presents the night as a time when God searched and tested David inwardly.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the statement, “thou hast visited me in the night”?

answers: He wants God's help to remain faithful and steady
He wants to leave God's paths
He wants to walk more quickly than his enemies
challenge.explanation: David depends on God to keep him from falling away from the right path.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David's request that his footsteps not slip?

answers: A plea to be heard, examination of his character, and a request for guidance
A description of wealth, a celebration, and a military victory
A complaint about the temple, a journey, and a feast
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from prayer, to testing, to faithfulness and guidance.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes David's words in verses 1–5?

paragraphs.title: A Call for Help and Protection

answers: Hear him
Give him a kingdom
Send him away
easy.explanation: David says, “I have called upon thee, for thou wilt hear me.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to do when he calls upon Him?

answers: His hidden treasure
His marvellous lovingkindness
His enemies' strength
easy.explanation: David asks God to show His “marvellous lovingkindness.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to show?

answers: Under the shadow of His wings
Inside a palace
Among the mountains
easy.explanation: David asks God to hide him “under the shadow of thy wings.”
easy.q: Where does David ask God to hide him?

answers: He calls because he wants God to listen and answer
He calls because he wants to flee from God
He calls to announce a victory
medium.explanation: David's prayer is a direct appeal for God's attentive response.
medium.q: What is the connection between David's call and his request that God incline His ear?

answers: Something precious that must be carefully protected
A high mountain
A hidden enemy
medium.explanation: The expression pictures careful and close protection.
medium.q: What does the expression “the apple of the eye” suggest in this passage?

answers: Both describe protection and watchful care
Both describe warfare
Both describe material prosperity
medium.explanation: David asks to be guarded as carefully as the eye and sheltered beneath wings.
medium.q: How do the images of the eye and the wings express a common idea?

answers: He needs God's personal answer as well as God's shelter
He doubts that God can hear him
He wants to manage without God's help
challenge.explanation: David seeks both communication with God and safety from those who oppose him.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David asking both to be heard and to be protected?

answers: Wings suggest a covering that shelters and protects
Wings represent great wealth
Wings describe enemies flying overhead
challenge.explanation: The image emphasizes refuge beneath a protective covering.
challenge.q: Why is the image of wings suitable for David's request for protection?

answers: David calls to God, asks for lovingkindness, and seeks shelter
David describes wealth, then asks for judgment
David describes enemies, then celebrates a feast
challenge.explanation: The passage develops from calling upon God to receiving His protection.

answers: His deadly enemies
His family
Those who trust in God
easy.explanation: David says that his deadly enemies “compass me about.”

answers: Proudly
Silently
Thankfully
easy.explanation: The verse says, “with their mouth they speak proudly.”
easy.q: How do the enemies speak with their mouths?

answers: An eagle
A lion
A deer
easy.explanation: The enemy is compared to a lion greedy for prey and a young lion lurking in secret places.
easy.q: To what animal is the enemy compared?

answers: They are focusing on their victim in order to attack
They are closing their eyes in fear
They are looking upward in prayer
medium.explanation: Their fixed eyes portray deliberate attention toward a target.
medium.q: What does the statement that the enemies have “set their eyes” suggest?

answers: They have surrounded and closed in on David
They have offered David a place of refuge
They have thanked David for his help
medium.explanation: The phrase describes enemies surrounding David wherever he goes.
medium.q: What does “compassed us in our steps” mean in context?

answers: He waits secretly and seeks prey
He protects the weak
He runs away from danger
medium.explanation: The lion represents a predator that lurks and prepares to seize its prey.
medium.q: How does the comparison to a lion explain the enemy's behavior?

answers: Both present them as forceful, threatening, and aggressive
Both show that they are weak and frightened
Both show that they are peaceful and quiet
challenge.explanation: Their proud words and hunting imagery combine to portray an intimidating enemy.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between the enemies' proud speech and their predatory conduct?

answers: David feels trapped and threatened from every side
David is enjoying a peaceful journey
The enemies have already gone away
challenge.explanation: The repeated surrounding imagery heightens the sense of danger and confinement.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repeated idea of being surrounded?

answers: They surround David, focus on their target, and are pictured as lurking predators
They flee, give thanks, and ask for protection
They rest, celebrate, and begin a journey
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the general threat of surrounding to the detailed image of a lion waiting for prey.
challenge.q: Which order best describes the enemies' presentation in this passage?

paragraphs.title: A Plea for Victory and Hope of Salvation

answers: Cast him down
Make him wealthy
Hide him
easy.explanation: David asks the LORD to “disappoint him” and “cast him down.”
easy.q: What does David ask the LORD to do to the wicked enemy?

answers: The wicked
The night
The wilderness
easy.explanation: David asks to be delivered from the wicked, who are described as God's sword.
easy.q: From whom does David ask God to deliver his soul?

answers: The face of God
The wealth of his enemies
A royal palace
easy.explanation: David says, “I will behold thy face in righteousness.”
easy.q: What does David hope to behold?

answers: They enjoy their portion in this life, while David hopes to see God's face
They seek God's shelter, while David seeks riches
They hide from danger, while David describes them as lions
medium.explanation: The passage contrasts earthly satisfaction with David's spiritual hope.
medium.q: How are the men of the world contrasted with David?

answers: He expects lasting satisfaction in God's presence and likeness
He wants food after sleeping
He describes the hunger of his enemies
medium.explanation: David's deepest satisfaction is connected with awakening to God's likeness.
medium.q: What does David mean by saying, “I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness”?

answers: Rescue from the wicked allows David to look forward to seeing God's face
Deliverance will give David worldly wealth
Deliverance will cause David to join his enemies
medium.explanation: David asks for immediate rescue while holding to the future hope of God's presence.
medium.q: How is the request for deliverance connected to the final verse?

answers: They are satisfied with earthly abundance, while David seeks satisfaction in God's presence
They seek God's face, while David seeks wealth
They are being hunted, while David describes them as lions
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts their portion in this life with David's desire for God's likeness.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the men of the world and David?

answers: His hope is connected with a life of righteousness before God
He wants to take personal revenge
He is describing the wealth of the wicked
challenge.explanation: The phrase links David's final hope with the righteousness he has claimed throughout the psalm.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “in righteousness” emphasize in David's hope to see God's face?

answers: The beginning asks God to judge David's righteousness, and the ending hopes to see God's face in righteousness
The beginning describes wealth, and the ending describes a battle
The beginning describes enemies, and the ending describes their birth
challenge.explanation: The psalm begins with a plea for righteous judgment and ends with hope of seeing God in righteousness.
challenge.q: How does the ending of the psalm connect with its beginning?
